title: CP2395-23 - Sexual Health & Reproductive Health Service
description:
The service aims to improve sexual and reproductive health outcomes and reduce health inequalities of Devon and Torbay residents. \r
\r
Devon County Council and Torbay Council required a system leader to manage and develop the sexual & reproductive health system across the two local authority areas. The system leader will forge critical partnerships with a range of clinical, voluntary, community and social enterprise sector organisations, commissioning organisations, and our local population to truly improve sexual and reproductive health and wellbeing of people, pathways and outcomes across Devon and Torbay. \r
\r
The integrated Sexual and Reproductive Health Service will be delivered by a single organisation or consortia across the administrative areas of Devon County Council and Torbay Council. Each Authority will hold a separate Contract with the successful Provider.\r
\r
This provision is being procured under The Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 following 'The Competitive Process' route (Regulation 11). \r
\r
This is a Provider Selection Regime (PSR) Contract Notice. The awarding of this contract is subject to the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. For the avoidance of doubt, the provisions of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 do not apply to this award.\r
\r
OPTION - Modifications:\r
Devon County Council and Torbay Council does not guarantee that additional funding for the Integrated Sexual and Reproductive Health Service in Devon and Torbay will be forthcoming. However, in the event that each council is able to secure additional funding up to £39,650,000 (£9,220,930 Torbay Council & £30,429,070 Devon County Council via a grant or other means) to form part of the Integrated Sexual and Reproductive Health Service for Devon and Torbay, commissioners would work with the provider(s) on the best way to allocate funding that increases capacity, accessibility or service quality in line with this specification in the areas of areas a) to e) and modifications outlined in Section 13 Table 1 of the specification. \r
 \r
a.	Sexual Health Promotion and Prevention  \r
b.	Online STI testing, treatment, partner notification and contraception (where clinically appropriate)  \r
c.	Specialist Integrated Sexual and Reproductive Health Service (L1-3)  \r
d.	Level 229 Enhanced Sexual and Reproductive Health Services through community settings (this will include, but is not limited to general practice and community pharmacy) \r
e.	Overall sexual and reproductive health system leadership, network management and training. \r
\r

- NHS England - South West House, Blackbrook Park Avenue, Taunton, TA1 2PX\r

title: CP2276-22 Road Weather Data Bureau Service for Devon Consortium (Devon County Council, Torbay Council and Plymouth City Council)
description:
Devon County Council (DCC), on behalf of the Devon Consortium, currently comprising Devon County Council, Torbay Council (TC) and Plymouth City Council (PCC), require a Road Weather Data Bureau Service so that they can deliver an effective and efficient Winter Service and Highway Maintenance function, reacting in a timely and appropriate fashion to any hazards that may be presented to highway users, in winter and support Highway Maintenance activities in the summer.

DCC currently has a network of 33 road weather stations, whilst Torbay Council has one and Plymouth City Council has three and has a reciprocal agreement to access weather stations from adjacent highways authorities. The weather stations are currently a combination of Vaisala (ROSA and later) and Findlay Irvine (Mk6 and later) supplied equipment, fitted with a range of meteorological and road sensors, and a number have the ability to transmit images.

Data is also received from a forecast provider. The primary aim of this procurement is to ensure that both actual and forecast data are integrated into visualization software which is accessible through web browsers. 

The Devon Consortium will access the bureau service as if one customer, but the individual logins shall provide suitable configuration to each separate Authorities requirement.  All data shall be freely made available across Devon Consortium.

Devon also has a control room where this information is monitored 24 hours a day, 7 days a week throughout the year, to support the winter service and a proportion of the data is monitored through the summer, to aid decisions on weather and temperature dependent highway maintenance activities. The control room is generally single staffed out of hours and data is accessed via the internet, this data is also accessed by staff across the county who are on duty both in and out of hours, at work and at other locations including home.

This is a business-critical service, resilience is vital, as timely data is used to monitor the road temperatures and state and determine if any change is required to the winter action and to maintain records for future use. This is fundamental to the Authority's legal defence of winter claims and the delivery of some statutory duties.

Data is also received from a forecast provider. The primary aim of this procurement is to ensure that both actual and forecast data are integrated into visualization software which is accessible through web browsers.

title: Direct Award of Contract to provide an  Adults Social Care Case Management System
description:
Torbay Council has direct awarded a contract for provision of its new Adults Services' Case
Management System (CMS), to the incumbent supplier of its Children's Services' System.                                                               This is a direct award, following the publication of a Voluntary ex ante transparency (VEAT)
notice (reference: 2025/S 000-000406 on 07th January 2025, and subsequent internal
approval to directly award the contract from Torbay Council's Cabinet.
The system will be used by Torbay Council and Torbay and South Devon NHS Foundation
Trust.
Award is made on the grounds that the works, supplies or services can only be provided by a
particular economic operator due to an absence of competition for technical reasons.
The Council undertook a further competition from Lot 3c of CCS' RM3821 Data &
Application Solutions Framework for a supplier for supply & ongoing maintenance of a
children's social care CMS. It allowed for the contract to be modified to include future
provision of an adult social care CMS, as the 2 systems are required to be compatible with
one another. The adult social care CMS was required after the Children's contract was
awarded. But due to unforeseen circumstances, including impact of COVID on social care
resources there was a significant delay in putting a new system in place. Due to this and
increases in the cost of the contract from the previously estimate, the Council considers that
it is no longer appropriate to modify the existing contract. However, a compatible system
across children's & adult's social care remains.
Whilst there are alternative suppliers of CMS's, appointment of a different supplier will result
in receiving a solution incompatible with the current children's CMS. The differences in how
the systems function will result in additional costs (to make each compatible with one
another), difficulties in implementing a new system and the ongoing operation / maintenance
of both, which will not deliver best value.
This direct award will deliver the following benefits to Council, the system's end users & the
public purse:
Seamless and more cost-effective integration with the current Children's CMS (Liquid Logic)
by utilising the same solution, and cost savings and efficiencies in hosting arrangements by
utilising the same supplier.
Efficiencies, consistency & effectiveness in reporting capabilities by utilising the same
solution and in contract management by having the same supplier for both CMS.
More efficient migration of data as, the same system used to be operated across both
children's & adult social care, meaning the Council's IT team have experience of migrating
data from the old system to the new.                                                                                                                                                          The Council will begin implementation planning and data migration from its current system, from July 2025 onwards

title: Torre Abbey Restoration Project
description:
Torbay Council is seeking a construction contractor with experience in Grade I / II, conservation, and heritage restoration for a restoration project at Torre Abbey.\r
\r
Torre Abbey is located, most unusually for a medieval monastery, on the seafront and is part of the Belgravia Conservation Area in Torquay. It comprises two Grade I listed buildings, four Grade II listed structures and ancillary buildings, an undesignated formal walled garden, all set in a Scheduled Ancient Monument, 17.8ha in extent (NHLE No. 1009302). The surrounding parkland contains earthworks and the remains of the abbey's precinct buildings, including a mill, stables, two watercourses (still flowing), and evidence of 18th / 19th century landscaping.  Exposure of this history, and its interpretation, will be a vital part of the landscape work in this third phase, reconnecting the abbey with its wider setting towards the seafront. \r
\r
Torre Abbey today is the most complete medieval monastery in Devon and Cornwall, and one of the best-preserved Premonstratensian houses in the UK.  Torre Abbey is one of four publicly owned art galleries in Devon.   The Spanish Barn is the only surviving prison for sailors of the Spanish Armada, which in 1588 united the country against Catholic Europe (hence its name).  \r
\r
Following the programmes of work in 2006 and 2011 much of the fabric has been repaired, and its condition secured for several decades to come. However, the poor state of remaining elements of the building imply risk and accelerating decline as leaking continues into fabric.  The following sections of building remain of concern, and form the basis of the repair project:\r
\r
â€¢	elevations of the south-east and south-west wings\r
â€¢	north elevation of west range\r
â€¢	gatehouse - these repair works have been postponed from previous phases 	of repair work and are now necessary to conserve the historic fabric and halt 	serious deterioration \r

title: Children's Residential Block Contract - Caring in Partnership
description:
Plymouth City Council is looking to procure a Children's Residential Home Block Contract, known as the Caring in Partnership contract. This ITT is issued as part of the procurement process.

The Caring in Partnership residential children's home block contract was first commissioned in 2018 and has been successful in securing and growing the number of children's homes operating within Plymouth and in being aspirational for the children placed. It has also contributed to successful partnership working between placement providers and the Council and its partners, and between providers themselves. The aim of the service is to provide local homes for local children, supported by a network of good quality provision and underpinned by partnership working across agencies. We want Plymouth children and young people to remain as close to the city as possible, and to be able to support those who are placed outside their home area to safely return.

Children and young people in the care of Plymouth City Council require a range of placements to meet their needs. Among these are residential children's homes, used for the most complex children and young people who struggle to manage the relationships in a family home. The Council wants to place in children's homes based on a model of care which is as close to a family environment as possible; with a consistent staff team skilled in working with children and young people with attachment difficulties and other challenges from adverse childhood experiences.

The work specified within this tender has been split into Lots

Lot 1 - Existing provision in and near to Plymouth

Lot 2 - Homes to be added to the contract at a later date

We are seeking to contract with a range of providers, both those who already have provision in or within 10 miles of the Plymouth city boundary, and those who wish to develop such provision. The spend for 2021 / 2022 on block contracted placements within the city boundary was approximately GBP 4million.

The Council is seeking to contract a maximum of 20 beds for Lot 1.

The contract will be managed through a range of meetings between the Council and providers and partners to encourage partnership working; these will include individual contract management meetings as well as group provider forums to share good practice and collectively resolve issues.

The following local authorities are parties to the contract and will be offered the option to express an interest in any vacant beds the Council is unable to fill

Torbay Council

Devon County Council

Somerset County Council

The anticipated duration of the contract is for 3 years plus options to extend on a 1 year + 1 year basis.

title: CP2412-23 Adoption Video Services

Adopt South West (ASW) Regional Adoption Agency (RAA) has been established to meet the government agenda for regionalising adoption as set out in the Education and Adoption Act 2016 more detail can also be found in the Department for Education (DfE) Regionalising Adoption June 2015 .\r
ASW operates across the Local Authority areas of Devon County Council, Plymouth City Council, Somerset Council and Torbay Council.\r
\r
ASW aims to improve the number of placements available for priority children.\r
\r
The provider of the service will support ASW's vision to achieve improved outcomes for children and families. ASW will create a system where children are matched with the most suitable adopter as quickly as possible, as part of this ASW are seeking to commission the service of the production of professional video recordings of certain children waiting for adoption.\r
\r
ASW will determine and identify those Children and Young People for whom the video recordings would be the most beneficial, this will, in the main, be for those Children and Young People who may be more difficult to place. This may for example be sibling groups, or individuals due to their age, or indeed complexity of need.\r
\r
The video recordings will be used in a number of ways to support the placement of children for adoption and permanence. For example, they will be shown at Family Finding evenings, and possibly through online portals. It is important to note that in line with best practice, all the video recordings must be appropriate for the Child to view, they will be shared with the child as part of their life story work at the appropriate time. They must also be sensitive towards the Child's family of birth due to the possibility that they may access it.

title: Mental Health Treatment Requirements (MHTRs) in Devon & Torbay for NHS England (NHSE) South West
description:
NHS England South West (the Commissioner)  sought to commission Mental Health Treatment Requirements (MHTRs) Services in Devon and Torbay. 

MHTRs form part of the wider Community Sentence Treatment Requirements (CSTRs) Programme which is a partnership between the Ministry of Justice (MoJ), Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC), NHS England (NHSE), Public Health England (PHE) and His Majesty's Prison and Probation Service (HMPPS).  

The CSTR Programme aims to develop pathways to enable and facilitate the increased use of all three treatment requirements:
-	Mental Health Treatment Requirements (MHTRs)
-	Drug Rehabilitation Requirements (DRRs)
-	Alcohol Treatment Requirements (ATRs)

ATRs and DRRs in Devon and Torbay were outside the scope of this procurement, beyond the co-ordination of CSTRs for combined orders. However, there is an expectation that MHTR and ATR & DRR providers will work closely together in the best interests of the service user, especially where it can be identified that a combined order is the best outcome.

MHTR in the context of the CSTR programme is intended for the sentencing of individuals convicted of an offence(s) which has crossed the community order sentencing threshold and may be used as an alternative to short custodial sentences for individuals who may have range of mental health, personality disorder and psychological issues/vulnerabilities, which do not require forensic or secondary care treatment.

The aims of the service are to:
•	Increase the proportion of offenders with mental health issues for whom an effective mental health treatment plan is in place.
•	Reduce re-offending by addressing the underlying causes of offending behaviour. 
•	Prevent custodial sentences (especially short ones), by offering robust community treatment options.
•	Provide tailored mental health support to the most vulnerable offenders. Individuals supported by pilot sites included those who suffered from post-traumatic stress, trauma, bipolar, personality and phobia disorders, psychosis and ASD. 

The contract will be for a term of 2 years and 1 month.

The financial envelope related to delivering an indicative volume of 150 MHTRs.

The Commissioner had a maximum budget available of up to £155,000 per annum and a total budget of up to £322,917 over the life of the contract. 

In addition to the funding for service delivery, up to £27,000 of mobilisation funding was available to support the process. 

Services commenced on 01 March 2023.

This procurement is being carried out by NHS South, Central and West Commissioning Support Unit (SCW) on behalf of the Commissioners.

title: CP2566-24 One Public Estate Co-location
description:
Devon and Torbay One Public Estate (managed by Devon County Council) wish to tender for a consultant to undertake a selection of public sector colocation opportunities and take forward those to business case stage or delivery dependant on the stage of the project named below -

- Phase 4 estates Restructure Devon County Council
- Colocation of NHS Properties - Through best practise visits
- Colocation of DCC / NHS into Follaton House / Forde House
- Colocation of DCC into Phoenix house Mid Devon
- Colocation of NHS /DCC into Kilworthy House
- Review of Key colocation opportunities in Ilfracombe / Barnstaple
- Review of key colocation opportunities Bideford .

The post-COVID-19 shift to hybrid working has significantly reduced the need for office space, with 65-85% of former office-based workers preferring remote work. This change necessitates a review of public sector office and front-facing space requirements.

The Devon and Torbay OPE Partnership has undertaken a review of their Estate and the requirements for a modern collocated public sector. The partnership examined the current public sector footprint in Devon, as well as the individual requirements of different services and departments within those services. Previous work has found that there were services across Devon with excess office / front facing space that was going unused as staff worked from home instead, and that there were several opportunities for the disposal of assets - often office building that were no longer fit-for-purpose - if staff were condensed into a reduced number of buildings. 

Furthermore, previous work found colocation opportunities that could free up critical clinical space, allow for greater partnership working across different authorities, and release land for housing. It also introduced the idea of shared, Family Hubs, where staff could use any public sector space of geographic proximity on a reciprocal basis.

title: CP2549-24: Devon and Somerset Standing List of Approved Contractors (SLoAC) 2025
description:
The Devon & Somerset Standing List of Approved Contractors (the SLoAC) provides a set of pre-qualified contractors for Maintenance, Improvement, and Building Works up to £2,000,000 per project, with most works ranging between £5,000 and £250,000, and for works below £5,000.\r
\r
SLoAC 2025 will replace the existing SLoAC, which has been in operation since 1st April, 2016, and will expire on 31 March, 2025. All interested contractors, including those currently on the existing list must re-apply to join SLoAC 2025. SLoAC 2025 is anticipated to commence April 2025, and will run for 4 years (Until 31st March 2029) with a break clause at the end of the second year (31 March 2027) and an option to extend for a further 4 years in 2 years increment (until 31 March 2033) at the Authority's discretion.\r
\r
The SLoAC will be re-opened periodically (anticipated to be annually) in order to enable contractors to apply to join the list. If in the Authority's reasonable opinion, specific work categories have sufficient numbers of contractors in a work category, the Authority reserves the right not to open those work categories to new applications to prevent having excessive numbers of contractors. In this initial application period no limit will be set to the number of contractors that will be accepted into a work category. The Authority also reserves the right to include additional works categories when the arrangement is reopened.\r
\r
Contractors will be appointed to the SLoAC based on achieving certain minimum standards through pass/fail questions. The award of specific projects will be subject to a competitive procurement process for each individual project. Only approved contractors on the SLoAC will get an opportunity to be selected to participate in a competitive processes when a needs arises. To be approved, contractors must obtain and maintain accreditation from our Comprehensive Accreditation Service Provider.. This is not a condition of joining the SLoAC but a condition for being selected to take part in a competitive process when a need arises.\r
\r
SLoAC is divided into 37 work categories, including 31 general and specialist categories,5 general agricultural categories, and a Principal Contractor category. Some of the most used work categories include Refurbishment and Repair, Heating, Roofing, Windows and Doors, New Build and Extension, and Agricultural Building - Build, Repair, and Maintenance. Contractors may apply for as many work categories as they wish to be active in.\r
\r
Devon has been subdivided into 8 geographical areas, plus the Torbay and Plymouth unitary authority areas, and Somerset into 5 geographical areas for the purpose of the SLoAC. Contractors may choose to operate in any number of these areas, subject to qualification.\r

title: CP2567-24 Adult Safeguarding & Mental Capacity Act Training
description:
Devon County Council (DCC) and Torbay and Devon Safeguarding Adults Partnership Board (TDSAP) are procuring for Adult Safeguarding Training and Mental Capacity Act Training.  \r
\r
The procurement is split into two lots, and two contracts will be awarded:\r
\r
Lot 1 - Adult Safeguarding Training (maximum budget £28,800 per annum)\r
Lot 2 - Mental Capacity Act Training (maximum budget £18,400 per annum)\r
\r
Suppliers can bid for one lot or two lots.\r
\r
This provision is being procured under Part 2, Chapter 3, Section 7 of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (PCR 2015) - Social and Other Specific Services (also known as 'the light touch regime') and this procurement does not follow, in particular, any of the defined procedures of the PCR 2015 (even if there are similarities) but does seek to adhere to the best practice procurement principles of Openness, Transparency, Fairness and Equity.

description:

SME AI Awareness Training is a Digital Skills Series training programme, designed to support SMEs to understand and explore the potential opportunities that AI adoption can provide to their organisation.\r
Funding has been allocated to provide 80 SME AI Awareness Training places.
